result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Each lane flowNodeRef identifies a node in the owning process. Assign nodes according to stated responsibility and avoid arbitrary membership.
Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Lanes may be nested: a lane can contain a child laneSet that partitions it further; every flowNodeRef at any depth references nodes of the one owning process.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

Each branch leads to a send task addressed to the one team responsible for that option. Do not send all options to all teams, and do not use a single send task for every option.

When the description says an outside party (such as a customer) chooses among several configuration options, with each option being a separate choice, and the options are sent to that party before its choices are received and before work is dispatched to other teams: Model the options being sent to the outside party as a sendTask. Model each option the party chooses as its own user task, placed after that send task and before the parallel split that dispatches the work. Keep every choice as a distinct element and do not merge them into one task.

When the description names two or more alternative activities joined by 'or' (for example, 'A or B' as the options the team may perform), and a decision follows that leads to one of them: Model each alternative activity as its own task on its own outgoing branch of the decision gateway, labeled with that alternative's own wording from the description. Do not merge the alternatives into one task whose label joins them with 'or'.

When the description states two alternative methods for the same activity, and the choice between them depends on a stated criterion or threshold (such as an amount or size) that is separate from an earlier yes/no decision about whether the activity happens at all: Model an exclusive (XOR) gateway at the point of choice, with one outgoing flow to each alternative method as its own task. Name the gateway with a question that states the selecting criterion from the description, not a repetition of the earlier decision's question. Route the alternatives into one exclusive merge only if the process continues afterwards.

result.rule: When The description says the process sends a request or places an order with an outside party, and the next step can only happen after that party's reply or confirmation arrives, without describing a decision based on that reply.: Model the wait for the reply or confirmation as an intermediate message catch event placed after the request activity and before the step that depends on it, connected by sequence flows in that order. Do not model the wait as a task, and do not leave it out so that the next step follows the request directly.

When the description says that the next step can only follow after a condition on collected responses or received results is reached, such as a number of people agreeing or a list having been received, and it states that step with 'until' or 'as soon as': Model an intermediate catch event between the activity that gathers the responses or results and the decision or step that uses them. Label the event with the condition as the description states it, and connect it with sequence flow so that the following decision or step continues from it. Do not omit the wait, and do not model it as a task.

When the description states that an outside party reviews the material the company has submitted and identifies issues in it, and that a later step carries out changes based on those findings, with no decision depending on the result: Model the outside party's review as its own task, labeled with the description's own wording for that review. Place it after the task or send task that submits the material and before the task that carries out the changes, and connect the three with sequence flows in that order. Do not merge the review into the submission task or the change task, and do not drop it.

When the description states that a participant outside the company performs an action, such as choosing or supplying information, and the process then depends on that action: Model a task for the participant's own action, labeled with the verb and object the description uses for what the participant does (for example, 'provide ...' or 'select ...'). Do not label the task with the organization's receipt or processing of that input, and do not merge a separately described participant action into a task for the organization's follow-up communication.
